interview.hardest_part: The finale sequence requiring me to steal the bell from the model village and return it to the starting area while navigating back through all previous areas, likely with NPCs interfering, all with discrete turn-based control in a real-time game
interview.likely_failure: Running out of wall-clock time in the mid-to-late game areas (pub or model village) due to the compounding effect of real-time gameplay continuing while I deliberate on each action, or getting stuck on timing-sensitive multi-step tasks that require observing NPC patterns across multiple frames
interview.helpful_mechanics: Fixed village layout allowing spatial learning, Tab key to review tasks, point-and-click movement not requiring precise analog control, and my prior knowledge of the game's general structure and puzzle types
interview.harmful_mechanics: Real-time gameplay consuming wall-clock time during my decision-making, single screenshot per turn preventing observation of motion and NPC behavior patterns, complex task dependencies requiring specific sequences that are hard to execute with discrete actions, and having only one attempt with no opportunity to learn from failures
